quest.title: The Oni's Justice
quest.description: You set off to Yashiori Island using the clues Sango provided...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x600, Mora x38100, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

talks.objective: Go to Yashiori Island to search for Arataki Itto
Use Elemental Sight to chase the tracks

dialogues.speaker: Daisuke
dialogues.text: Please, you gotta believe me! Uncle Itto didn't do anything wrong, he's not a bad guy!

dialogues.speaker: Granny Oni
dialogues.text: I'll take care of Daisuke. No need to worry, dear. Everything will be fine.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, could that be him? Is that Arataki Itto?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He doesn't seem to be looking this way. Perfect, let's try the beans Detective Sango gave us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It'll save a lot of hassle if we can avoid a fight.

talks.objective: Hit Arataki Itto with the beans

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: By the way, Paimon's curious... What kind of game is beetle fighting?

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: You guys have seen Onikabuto out in the wild, right? Even though they might look menacing on the outside, they're big softies on the inside. Most of the time they just sit there doing nothing.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: But let me tell ya, once the Onikabuto start fighting, they won't let anything get in their way!

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: The grand game of beetle fighting is a match where your beetle tries to flip the other beetle onto its back.

choices.text: I played when I was a kid.

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Hey, it's not just some kids game, okay? It's way deeper than you think!

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: I have taken part in more beetle fights than you would believe. At least 800 — I may have even crossed the thousand mark by this point. Anyway, after a while, you can tell a beetle's fighting potential just by looking at its shape, size, and the patterns on its body.

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: But it's not just about all the physical stuff, oh no! Your Onikabuto's gotta be in the right headspace as well. If it's not up for a fight or doesn't have the guts, then it's game over.

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Haha! Boy, are you two lucky you ran into me. When it comes to beetles, I'm the expert that the experts go to! I'll show you all you need to know.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But, we're not the ones that will be playing... We're just here to keep an eye on you.

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: ...Oh yeah.

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Anyway, not a problem! You two might think that I'm just tooting my own horns here, but just you wait... I'll make you a beetle expert in no time!

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: And by the way, that kid has one tough beetle, we can't underestimate it. We have to find a real lean mean beetle warrior.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, he's not the sharpest horn on the oni...

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Okay, lemme see...

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: There. Let's head to that hill. I'll bet my bottom Mora we're gonna find some major-league Onikabuto hiding out there.

choices.text: I watched people playing that when I was a kid.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: *whimpering*

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, are you okay?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What should we do? Paimon didn't think he'd react this badly!

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: D—Don't be alarmed... It's just my allergies acting up... I've got it under control!

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: It's alright, I got this, just gotta tough it out. I can take it... I can take it...

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Ah! Who am I kidding! *coughing* I gotta catch my breath here! *coughing* Whatever it is you want, it's gonna have to wait! I need a moment...

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Ahh, whew... that's better. That sure took a lot out of me, though...

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Hey, why'd you have to be so mean, huh!? Surprise-attacking me like that!

choices.text: You can never be too careful when dealing with a fugitive.

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Oh, I get it. So you're here to bring me in. How in the world did you find me all the way out here?

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Heh, well, whatever... If you think I'm going back with you, you can forget it. I'd walk away if I were you.

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: I pack a mean punch, you know. I don't want to hurt any regular folks like you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's pretty big talk considering all the beans we have.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You're the one behind the robbery and the missing people, aren't you?

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Yep, that's right. Me! All by myself. Nobody else.

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: As boss of the Arataki Gang, I gotta nab a little food and drink when we're running low. That's only natural, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, but nabbing people? That's taking it a bit far, don't ya think?

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Uh... not when their families will pay good Mora to see them again! Easy pickings.

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: And the extra Mora means I can... uh, give some to my gang to spend on themselves!

choices.text: At least you're honest.

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Hey, what's with all the questions? Like I said, I'm not going back with you, so stop wasting everybody's time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No way, mister! We've accepted a commission to bring you back.

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: What'd you say, little one? Go on... Say it to my face!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Uh, we... Well, mostly {F#she}{M#he}, took a commission to bring you back.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Show some backbone, Paimon...

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Looks like you aren't gonna let this drop. In that case, we—
Uncle Itto!

response.speaker: Granny Oni
response.text: Don't run, now! Careful or you'll fall.

response.speaker: Daisuke
response.text: What's taking you so long? You said we were gonna have a beetle fight today! C'mon, you promised!

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Ah, y—yeah, that's right, still going ahead! But you see, uh... I've been out here for ages and I still can't find a beetle that I like. Just give Uncle Itto a little more time, m'kay?

response.speaker: Daisuke
response.text: Huh? Who are they? Are they your friends?

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Uh, yeah, that's right. I told them not to come, but what can I say? ... They were just too worried about me! Hahaha.

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: It's 'cause of a little thing called, uh... prestige, yeah. 'Cause of all the prestige Uncle Itto has.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? What are you talking about? We...

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Shh! C'mon. Just play along! Leave the kid out of this.

response.speaker: Daisuke
response.text: Uh, Uncle Itto, you don't look so good. You look like you're about to fall over.

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Hehe, that's because Uncle Itto bumped his noggin on a tree branch while looking for a beetle. It's all good, though, these horns are rock solid...

response.speaker: Daisuke
response.text: Okay, if you say so. Granny and I will keep heading back now. Don't be too long!

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Hehe, yep I'll be right there. I hope you're ready to lose today!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Who were those people?

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: The old lady was Granny Oni. She's the one that took me in and raised me. And the kid's name is Daisuke, I took him in just a while back. They're both like family to me.

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: They escaped with me out this way, along with my boys from the Arataki Gang. If I didn't bring them with me, the Tenryou Commission would be knocking on their doors, for sure.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I had no idea you were so caring towards others.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right, but if you care about them so much, then you shouldn't have done all that stuff that made them worry about you in the first place.

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: I, uh...

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Listen, how about we make a deal. You two let me go wrap things up with Daisuke, and once we're done battling beetles, the two of us will settle things with a duel.

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: If you win, I'll come quietly. You can take me back to Inazuma City, and you won't hear a peep outta me. Why? 'cause I'm an oni of my word.

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: I'll just tell little Daisuke that my friends and I need to step outside for a moment. That way, he won't worry. Cool?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Hmm, what should we do, {NICKNAME}? There is the kid to consider...

choices.text: Alright, you have a deal.

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Oh it's on! Heh, I like your style, haha! Alright, but first thing's first, I need to find an Onikabuto to battle with. I've been looking here for ages and haven't found myself a winner yet, so it's time to try somewhere else.

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Come with me. Saves you worrying that I might skedaddle.

choices.text: Either way, you won't escape.
Questionable reasoning there.
There's plenty more beans in the bag. You'd better come quietly.

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Hey, hey, take it easy... just stop with the beans, okay. So you're here to bring me in. How in the world did you find me all the way out here, anyway?

talks.objective: Go to the Onikabuto capture spot

dialogues.speaker: Daisuke
dialogues.text: Finally! You're back! Can we start our beetle fight now?

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Yeah, sure thing, buddy! But you'd better watch out, I brought a real winner back this time.

dialogues.speaker: Daisuke
dialogues.text: Don't worry, I'm not scared of your beetle. Go, go, Stripy Ghost!

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: I've got this fight in the bag! Let's go, Nimble Ninja!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? When did you come up with that name?

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: C'mon, you can take 'im, little guy!

dialogues.speaker: Daisuke
dialogues.text: Haha! That's right, finish it!

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Ah, no!!! My little Nimble Ninja!

dialogues.speaker: Daisuke
dialogues.text: Hah! Looks like I win again!

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Dang it, that's my seventh loss in a row!

choices.text: That is a poor track record...

response.speaker: Daisuke
response.text: Hee-hee, Stripy Ghost is invincible. Even Uncle Itto can't beat him!

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: I won't forget this! I'll beat you next time, I swear!

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Alright, Paimon, you're up. Time to give Crimson Cyclone a shot, maybe it'll end this losing streak of mine.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright! Go get 'em, Crimson Cyclone!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That name caught on quick.

response.speaker: Daisuke
response.text: Whoa! That one looks ultra strong!

response.speaker: Daisuke
response.text: But it's still no match for you, Stripy!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe! Alright little guy, use your Super Paimon Tornado!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...That's a real thing now!?

response.speaker: Daisuke
response.text: No, I can't believe it... I lost.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yay, we won! Hah, Paimon knew Crimson Cyclone would be the best!

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Boy, did that one put up a fight. It wiped the floor with Stripy Ghost...

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Heh, I know a real beetle trainer when I see one. Way to kick some beetle butt, partner!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hee-hee, see? Paimon's got real talent! Of course, Crimson Cyclone has to take some of the credit too...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Why don't we let Daisuke keep Crimson Cyclone?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh right, yeah, now that the beetle fighting's over and all...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This is for you, Daisuke.

response.speaker: Daisuke
response.text: Huh, for me? You're really giving it to me?

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Go ahead, take it, Daisuke. When we finally get back to the city, you can show it off to all your friends.

response.speaker: Daisuke
response.text: But... will we ever be able to go back?

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Of course we will, trust me. I never go back on my word!

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Anyway, I got some things I gotta discuss with my friends here. Go play with Granny for a while, would ya? There's a good boy!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Good, the kid doesn't suspect a thing...

response.speaker: Daisuke
response.text: You're from the Tenryou Commission, aren't you? I bet you're here to capture Uncle Itto.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh?

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Hey! Didn't I tell ya? They're my friends! ...Uh, in fact, they're in the gang. We're practically family!

response.speaker: Daisuke
response.text: That's not true! I already know everyone in your little gang, but I've never seen these two before!

response.speaker: Daisuke
response.text: Uncle Itto didn't do anything wrong, don't take him away!

response.speaker: Daisuke
response.text: And not only did he not do anything wrong, he also saved my life! He's not a bad guy!

choices.text: So what's the story here?

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Hey, some things we don't tell to outsiders, remember? *sigh* How should I explain...

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: I'm a real lousy liar...

response.speaker: Granny Oni
response.text: Itto, sometimes you need to just say what you have to say. Don't worry about us.

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: I guess... Thanks, Granny.

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Seems I can't hide it anymore. Come with me, I'll explain everything.

choices.text: Let's try to stay calm.
Seems Ogura Mio wasn't kidding.

talks.objective: Go to the tree where the Onikabuto reside

dialogues.speaker: Sango
dialogues.text: Thanks for your patronage and good luck!

dialogues.speaker: Sango
dialogues.text: Don't forget to come with a bigger budget next time.

talks.objective: Check the area where lightning struck
Leap off the gorge to look for Onikabuto

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: This is the one, this is the one! Hahaha! See? As long as you're in my company, you're guaranteed to find yourself an Onikabuto.

choices.text: It seems a bit different from the others.

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Yeah, it's on the smaller side. But size isn't everything in a beetle fight.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: But you said earlier that size matters...

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Just let the expert explain, okay? What smaller beetles lack in strength they make up for in agility. They usually got a whole bunch o' sick moves just ready to whip out when the right moment comes.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sure, but it doesn't seem to be very energetic, either.

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Listen, you can never see a beetle's true energy until it's in the ring.

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: It might look a bit young and docile, but that's got its advantages. Haven't you ever heard the saying, "Don't judge a book by its cover"?

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Young beetles that have never fought before always go all out in their first fight. Older beetles that have already been through the wars tend to just cower in the corner the moment they see a strong opponent.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I was hoping we'd catch a larger beetle.

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Hey, didn't I say not to worry! C'mon, just have a little faith, would ya? My experience is telling me that this Onikabuto was spawned to be a champion.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Wait a sec, where's Paimon?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right here! Look what Paimon found!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If we're gonna battle some beetles, then Paimon wants in! It's not like we have anything else to do... When you hopped down, Paimon flew off somewhere else nearby and found this one.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whaddya think, Itto? It's big and strong and looks like a real fighter. It matches everything you said about a good fighter beetle!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Bet the one you guys found must be way, way...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...b—bigger.

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Oh uh... Heh. You got some experience catching beetles too, huh?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nope, this is the first one Paimon's ever caught!

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Well, looks like you've got a real knack for this. You'll be a fellow beetle fighting expert in no time! I mean, not as good as me, but still.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh... so overall not that good, then.

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Uh anyway, great! With both your beetle and mine, I can tell this'll finally be the one! This time, I'm gonna win for sure!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: "This'll finally be the one"? ...You've never won before?

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Well, ahem... Y'know, that's just life, man. There are so many people in this world who are talented... and passionate... but it's no guarantee that things will go their way.

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: So many unrelated things have to come together at once in just the right way to make victory happen. There's this word that really sums it up nicely, actually. It's, uh, "co-incidence"!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: As in, pure luck...? Guess it makes no difference whether we have Paimon's beetle or not, then. Might as well just...

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Whoa whoa whoa, hey! Hehe, let's not do anything rash here!

choices.text: I thought smaller beetles know a bunch of sick moves?

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: I think both of these fine beetles have a shot at winning. Let's just hang on to them and give 'em both a try. A true warrior never leaves a good beetle behind, hahaha.

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Anyway — time to head back and get this show started! Man, I am psyched for this, wooh! Let's go!

choices.text: Didn't you say that younger beetles are fearless?
It's kinda... small.

talks.objective: Go have a bug battle with Daisuke and Itto
Learn about the Oni race's past from Itto

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: I'll be honest with you. This thing the Tenryou Commission is investigating, with someone going around taking people and their possessions... It wasn't me. Any of it.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: I have my own reasons for lying about it, and I really didn't want to get innocent people caught up in this while I'm still trying to solve the real problem here.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: I'm the same as you. I just wanna avoid conflict at all costs... But it's just not worth it if someone gets hurt.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So why in the world would you say that you're the culprit?

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: *sigh* Maybe you don't know because you're outlanders... It all started a long, long time ago with the story of the crimson oni and the blue oni...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hold on a second, if you're talking about that fairytale, we've heard that one already.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Oh, so you already know. Well, that makes things a whole lot easier.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... is the story from the fairytale really true?

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Everything about the fate of the oni is true. The blue oni chose exile, and the crimson oni stayed behind.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: But the other details aren't historically accurate. Fairytales are nice stories, but there's something they leave out... it's a little thing called the cold, hard truth.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: The Inazuma of long ago was a dangerous place. If you wanted the Raiden Shogun's protection, you had to have a good relationship with the humans.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: The oni are a proud kind, so it wasn't easy for them to ask others for acceptance. Over time, the oni eventually split into two factions.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: The crimson oni were friendly with the humans, but the blue oni, they were more stubborn and insisted on keeping to their own.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon thought you were two different species. So really, you're all one family?

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Yep, that's right. There's no real difference between us. We just paint our horns different colors to show which side we belong to.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So why did the blue oni choose to exile themselves?

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Because humans were still wary of oni at the time.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: The crimson oni always hoped to find a way to live in peace with the humans, but the blue oni kept clashing with them.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Humans didn't see a difference between crimson and blue oni. All they knew was that oni were hard to get along with.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: If things were to continue that way, the oni were never going to get along with humans. And so, the most revered leaders of the crimson and blue oni decided to resolve it once and for all.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Over drinks, they swore an oath. The blue oni would play the role of evil oni to help the crimson oni integrate into human society. But the blue oni's leader gave two conditions.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm? What were they?

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: First, the oni must abandon any prejudice they held against humanity. Every oni was to accept humans in their heart before the humans accepted them. Oni were not to use their strength to mistreat humans but also were not to stand for mistreatment against themselves.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Second, the crimson oni were to integrate with human society — but not by trying to please the humans. The oni were to embrace their own honest characters, surging tempers, and awesome strength to win respect from humans.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: In other words, they were to carry on the oni bloodline while also protecting our oni pride.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hmm, I see...

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: After choosing exile, the number of blue oni began to dwindle, until they eventually disappeared altogether.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Since I first heard the story of the blue and crimson oni as a kid, I've heard it countless times in my life... Not once did I ever imagine that the blue oni clan had actually survived...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So you're saying the real culprit was a descendant of the blue oni?

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: That's right. Most people don't pay attention to the color of an oni's horns. They probably don't even know that blue oni exist.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: But nothing gets by the Arataki Gang. At the scene of the crime, they saw an oni with different color horns than mine.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Still, it'd be strange if the culprit really was a descendant of the blue oni. I can't bring myself to accept it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Because the blue oni also value their own pride?

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Exactly! They would give up their life before abandoning their pride.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: I have always respected the blue oni for the sacrifice they made, and I know the aspirations my ancestors had for the future of all oni.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Our pride does not allow for any wrongdoing. You don't steal from other people, you don't harm other people, period!

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: My guess is that the blue oni was tricked or forced into it somehow. But I don't have any evidence...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So you're trying to buy more time?

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: That's right. If I didn't step in, then the Tenryou Commission would've definitely caught them by now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But what does Daisuke have to do with any of this? He said that you saved him, so he knows your story, right?

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: He was the one I managed to save from the ronin after I sent them running from the scene.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: He was off playing somewhere when they came by and ransacked his house. By the time he came back, his parents had been taken.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: The whole reason I'm in this is to help this kid find his mom and dad again.

choices.text: Why didn't you just tell us that in the first place?

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: I never wanted to tell you any of this... Heh, my original plan was to knock you both out and take my family to hide somewhere else.

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: There's more to this than just one blue oni — there's a dangerous group behind everything that's been going on. So I didn't want to get anyone else caught up in this mess.

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: That's everything, the whole story. If you still don't believe me and wanna drag me back to Inazuma City, then I'm going to fight you with all I've got.

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: But if you're willing to believe me, then please. Give me a little time. Once I find the blue oni, I'll turn the both of us in.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I will help you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yep, Paimon too!

choices.text: The real culprits must be brought to justice.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Just treat it like we're here to keep an eye on you.

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: So you... Heh, alright! I knew you'd be reasonable, I knew it! I was thinking right from the start — these two fine folks, they're just out here in the pursuit of truth and justice, man. We are gonna get along just great!

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: I should tell you though, things could get a little dangerous, so be ready for anything. Heh, don't say that I didn't warn you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, don't worry about us. We're seasoned adventurers!

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Alright, then our first job is to investigate where this blue oni is hidin' out. There's a victim of his that saw him up close currently taking refuge at Sangonomiya's camp. I figure we can start by talkin' to him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
